reason: This is a good race-week reply. It answers the question straight away: no 16-miler on Wednesday. It also explains why. The long runs are already done, and heavy legs with no pain are normal taper fatigue clearing. That speaks to her worry about losing fitness without brushing it aside. It gives her a small dose of race feel instead: 2 miles at marathon pace inside a 5-mile run. The 8:35 pace matches her 3:45 goal. The week stays light and follows her schedule. Monday and Friday are rest days, the runs are short and easy with heart-rate caps, and Saturday is a 2-mile shakeout in race shoes and kit. The race plan starts conservatively at 8:45 to 8:50 before settling at 8:35, which is sensible after a 4:02 debut. Volume drops well below the 34 miles she just ran, so the tiredness is handled. Nothing hurts, so no referral is needed. No must-never check is triggered. Every day is clear enough to run as written.
